description: Central -> daemon: open a port-forwarding tunnel through the third-party provider (P11, ADR 0022). This is the ONLY protocol message that carries a secret (`credential`), so it must never be logged and its golden fixtures use obviously fake values. There is deliberately no host, url, scheme or ssh option field: the provider host is a daemon-side constant and the target is always the node's own loopback, so this frame cannot be used to make a node connect somewhere of Central's choosing.

credential.description: Provider token, held by the platform and delivered per open (ADR 0022 D18). The character set is a security control, not tidiness: this value is concatenated into ssh's `<token>@<host>` argument, where Pinggy separates modifiers with `+` and the host with `@`. A value containing `+tcp` would change the tunnel type; one containing `@evil.host` would change the destination. Omitted on the free tier.

basic_auth.description: Provider-enforced HTTP basic auth (remote option b:user:pass). Neither field may contain ':' because that is the option's own separator - a colon would silently create a second credential pair or an unintended option.

allowed_ips.description: Provider-enforced source IP allowlist (remote option w:). Plain addresses or CIDR only; the option is comma-separated, so no element may contain a comma.

rewrite_host.description: Opt-in Host rewrite (remote option u:Host:localhost:<port>), default false. Measured in PG-01: the app otherwise receives the tunnel domain as Host, which dev servers with host allowlists (Vite, Next) refuse. Off by default because rewriting Host makes the app's own absolute URLs point at loopback.
